[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#FFA500][bold]COMMANDER & CHIEF ENFORCER PRIVILEGES[/bold][/color] ───────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
In the case where there is no Chief Enforcer stationed, or the Chief Enforcer is incapacitated or unavailable for an extended period of time, Enforcers are to also use this chain of command to determine the acting Commander.
- Chief Enforcer - Warden - Patrol Team Leader - Combat Medic - Enforcer - Junior Enforcer
The Chief Enforcer has significantly more power than an acting Commander. The Chief Enforcer also inherits also all privileges that a Commander would have by default. A Commander that is not also the Chief Enforcer may use any Chief Enforcer-specific privileges.
A Commander has the following privileges: - Change the sector's DEFCON level. - Declare a No Fly Zone. - Write and sign a search or arrest warrant.
The Chief Enforcer has the following privileges: - The ability to sign for and allow Class 2 Contraband permits. - Conduct warrantless searches with sufficient reasonable suspicion. - Open new TDF positions outside of the default allotted slots established by TDF High Command. - Use and access the TDF Auric Outpost account to pay staff and fund operations.
